percentage_cpu.why: Sustained high CPU indicates the VM is undersized or runaway processes are degrading the workload.

available_memory_bytes_mbytes.why: Low available memory causes paging and process kills, hurting reliability.

available_memory_bytes.why: Low available memory causes paging and process kills, hurting reliability.

os_disk_iops_consumed_percentage.why: Disk IOPS saturation throttles the VM and slows every dependent service.

network_in_total.why: Abnormal inbound traffic can signal an incident or a misbehaving client.

network_out_total.why: A spike in outbound traffic can signal data exfiltration, a runaway backup/replication job, or a chatty dependency — and on metered egress it drives cost.

slots_http5xx.why: 5xx responses mean users are seeing failures — the single clearest availability signal.

slots_httpresponsetime.why: Slow responses degrade UX and often precede outright failures.

cputime.why: High CPU time signals the plan is undersized for the load.

slots_healthcheckstatus.why: Failing instance health checks remove capacity and risk an outage.

cpupercentage.why: A saturated plan throttles every app hosted on it.

memorypercentage.why: Memory pressure on the plan causes restarts across all hosted apps.

availability.why: Any availability dip on storage cascades to everything that depends on it.

fileservices_availability.why: Any availability dip on storage cascades to everything that depends on it.

blobservices_successe2elatency.why: High end-to-end storage latency slows every read/write across dependent apps. Compare against server latency below to tell storage-side slowness from client/network.

blobservices_successserverlatency.why: Server latency is the storage-side processing time only. High server latency points at the storage tier (large ops, archive/cool reads, onset of throttling); high E2E but normal server latency points at the client/network instead.

throttling.why: AuthenticationError (403) is the OTHER half of access failures, distinct from AuthorizationError: it's a network-ACL/firewall deny (public access disabled or default action Deny), an invalid/expired SAS token, or a wrong account key — the request is rejected before authorization is even evaluated. This is the single most common 'storage reports 100% available but the app can't reach it' outage, so it must be caught separately from RBAC-style AuthorizationError.

fileservices_transactions.why: AuthenticationError (403) is the OTHER half of access failures, distinct from AuthorizationError: it's a network-ACL/firewall deny (public access disabled or default action Deny), an invalid/expired SAS token, or a wrong account key — the request is rejected before authorization is even evaluated. This is the single most common 'storage reports 100% available but the app can't reach it' outage, so it must be caught separately from RBAC-style AuthorizationError.

usedcapacity.why: UsedCapacity is the total bytes stored. A sudden climb can signal a runaway producer, a stuck lifecycle/cleanup job, or unbounded log/blob growth — worth watching before it drives cost or hits a quota.

node_cpu_usage_percentage.why: CPU-saturated nodes evict pods and degrade the whole cluster.

node_memory_working_set_percentage.why: Memory pressure triggers OOM kills and pod restarts.

kube_node_status_condition.why: NotReady nodes silently shrink capacity and risk an outage.

availability.why: If the vault is unavailable, every app that fetches secrets/keys at runtime breaks.

serviceapilatency.why: Slow vault calls add latency to app startup and token refresh.

saturationshoebox.why: Approaching the vault's transaction limits leads to throttling and failures.

serviceapiresult.why: 429 responses mean the vault is hitting its per-vault transaction limits; callers should cache secrets and back off, and heavy workloads may need to spread load across vaults.

backendhealthpercentage.why: Unhealthy backends behind Front Door cause user-facing errors.

totallatency.why: Edge latency directly impacts every request routed through Front Door.

originhealthpercentage.why: Unhealthy origins behind Front Door produce user-facing 5xx errors.

percentage5xx.why: 5xx at the edge means users are seeing failures right now.

dipavailability.why: Failing backend probes remove targets and can black-hole traffic.

vipavailability.why: VIP unavailability is a direct front-end outage.

normalizedruconsumption.why: NormalizedRUConsumption is the MAX RU utilization across partition key ranges as a percent of provisioned (or autoscale-max) RU/s. Sustained values near 100% mean a single partition is saturated — requests there get 429-throttled even while the account average looks fine. This is the earliest, truest signal of a hot partition or an under-provisioned container. Note: this is a provisioned/autoscale metric — SERVERLESS accounts don't emit it (there is no provisioned RU/s to normalize against), so on serverless it reads 'no data' and you should watch server-side latency and 429s instead.

totalrequests.why: A 429 means Cosmos rejected the request for exceeding the provisioned RU/s for that partition (or the serverless ceiling). The SDK retries with backoff, but sustained 429s surface to the app as added latency and eventually failures — the direct signal that the data tier is over its throughput budget.

serversidelatency.why: ServerSideLatency is the time Cosmos itself spent servicing the request (excludes network and SDK). Rising server latency points at expensive cross-partition queries, missing indexes, or large documents — tuning targets that no amount of client-side scaling fixes.

totalrequestunits.why: 429s mean the container is over-provisioned RU/s limits and requests fail.

serviceavailability.why: Any Cosmos availability dip directly impacts the application's data tier.

serverload.why: A saturated Redis server slows or drops cache operations for dependent apps.

usedmemorypercentage.why: Memory pressure triggers eviction and breaks cache-dependent flows.

unhealthyhostcount.why: Unhealthy backends behind the gateway cause user-facing failures.

failedrequests.why: A rise in failed requests signals backend or capacity problems.

capacity.why: High gateway capacity means APIM is near saturation and will start throttling.

failedrequests.why: Gateway 5xx errors break every API consumer behind APIM.

backendduration.why: Slow backends behind APIM degrade all routed APIs.

percentage_cpu.why: Sustained high CPU across instances means the scale set is undersized.

available_memory_bytes.why: Low memory causes paging and instance instability.

restartcount.why: Frequent replica restarts indicate crash-looping revisions (bad image, failing readiness probe, or OOM).

replicas.why: Replicas is the current replica count. Pinned at the max scale bound under load means the app is capacity-capped (raise maxReplicas or the scale rule); flapping to zero explains cold-start latency on the next request.

usagenanocores.why: Absolute CPU consumption in nanocores — a raw companion to CpuPercentage for sizing.

storageused_for_standard_pricing_plan.why: Approaching the registry storage quota blocks new pushes.

storageused.why: Approaching the registry storage quota blocks new pushes.

elasticpools_dtu_consumption_percent.why: A saturated elastic pool throttles every database in it.

cpu_percent.why: Sustained high CPU throttles queries and stalls the application.

memory_percent.why: Memory pressure causes slow queries and connection failures.

storage_percent.why: A full data disk takes the server read-only — a write outage.

connections_failed.why: A rise in failed connections signals auth, limit, or capacity problems.

cpu_percent.why: Sustained high CPU throttles queries and stalls the application.

memory_percent.why: Memory pressure causes slow queries and connection failures.

storage_percent.why: A full data disk takes the server read-only — a write outage.

aborted_connections.why: Aborted connections signal client, auth, or capacity issues.

servererrors.why: Server errors mean the namespace is failing requests from producers/consumers.

throttledrequests.why: Throttling means the namespace is over its limits and messages are rejected.

deadletteredmessages.why: Growing dead-letter queues mean messages can't be processed — data is stuck.

activemessages.why: A growing backlog signals consumers can't keep up with the producers.

usererrors.why: UserErrors are client-side failures (bad auth, message-too-large, entity-not-found, lock lost). Unlike ServerErrors they point at the producer/consumer code or config — a spike usually means a recent deploy broke how the app talks to the namespace.

servererrors.why: Server errors mean events are being rejected by the namespace.

throttledrequests.why: Throttling means ingestion is over the provisioned throughput units.

capturebacklog.why: A capture backlog means events aren't landing in storage on time.

quotaexceedederrors.why: QuotaExceededErrors mean producers/consumers hit a hard namespace quota (throughput-unit ceiling, connection count, or entity size). Events are rejected outright — a sharper signal than generic throttling that the tier is undersized for the load.

incomingmessages.why: IncomingMessages is the ingest rate. Read alongside ThrottledRequests it shows whether a throttle is driven by real volume (scale up TUs) or a hot partition (fix the partition key).

outgoingmessages.why: OutgoingMessages is the consumer egress rate. Persistently far below IncomingMessages means consumers are falling behind — the lag that eventually breaches retention and loses events.

publishfailcount.why: Publish failures mean producers can't emit events.

deadletteredcount.why: Dead-lettered events were never delivered to any subscriber.

deliveryattemptfailcount.why: Failed deliveries mean subscribers aren't receiving events.

runsfailed.why: Failed runs mean the workflow's business process isn't completing.

actionlatency.why: High action latency slows the end-to-end workflow.

snatportutilization.why: SNAT port exhaustion silently drops outbound connections across the whole network.

throughput.why: Approaching the firewall throughput ceiling adds latency and risks drops.

firewallhealth.why: A degraded firewall can black-hole or bottleneck all routed traffic.

ifunderddosattack.why: An active DDoS attack on the public IP threatens the availability of the front-end.

clienterrors.why: 429s mean requests are exceeding the deployment's TPM/RPM quota and failing.

latency.why: High inference latency degrades every dependent experience.

servererrors.why: 5xx errors from the AI service break inference calls.

throttledsearchqueriespercentage.why: Throttled queries mean the service is over capacity and dropping requests.

searchlatency.why: Slow search hurts every search-driven experience.

failed_runs.why: Failed runs mean training/scoring jobs aren't completing.

quota_utilization_percentage.why: Compute quota exhaustion blocks new jobs from starting.

pipelinefailedruns.why: Failed pipelines mean data isn't moving — downstream reports/ETL go stale.

triggerfailedruns.why: Failed triggers mean scheduled pipelines never started.

activityfailedruns.why: Failed activities point to the specific step breaking a pipeline.

throttledhttprequestcount.why: ThrottledHttpRequestCount is requests rejected with 429 for exceeding the store's request quota (the Free tier caps daily requests hard, Standard caps per-second). Throttling means apps can't read their configuration/feature flags at runtime — startup stalls and flags go stale. The fix is client-side caching/Sentinel polling or moving off Free.
